text: Was B’s transfer caused by a deliberate action by A?
Did A’s deliberate action directly target B, rather than causing B to transfer as an indirect consequence?
Did A’s deliberate action lead the school to make a decision that caused B to transfer?
Was the decision for B to transfer made by B or someone close to B?
Did A’s action cause the transfer through an effect on someone other than B?
Did A’s action also cause another person to transfer schools?
Was the person affected by A’s action personally connected to B?
Was the person affected by A’s action related to B?
Was the person affected by A’s action an immediate family member of B?
Did the family member’s reaction to A’s action prompt B to transfer?
Did the family member’s own subsequent relocation lead B to transfer?
Did A’s action cause B’s family member to face a serious consequence that changed B’s circumstances?
Was the serious consequence a legal consequence for B’s family member?
Was the legal consequence for B’s family member criminal in nature, rather than civil or administrative?
Did the criminal consequence include B’s family member actually being imprisoned, rather than only being investigated, arrested, or charged?
Did B’s family member actually commit the crime that led to the criminal consequence?
Did A’s action cause the family member to commit the crime, rather than expose or report a crime they had already committed?
Did A’s action bring the family member’s already-committed crime to the attention of the authorities?
Did A deliberately give authorities information that exposed the family member’s already-committed crime?
Did A’s disclosure cause B to face stigma or bullying that prompted B to transfer schools?
Did the criminal consequence leave the family member unable to care for B?
Did the family member’s criminal consequence change B’s living situation in a way that prompted the transfer?
Was the family member whose crime A exposed one of B’s parents?
Was the parent whose crime A exposed B’s father?
Did A actually kill B?
Did the parent’s legal consequences cause B to move into a different household, prompting the transfer?
Did B move in with a relative after the parent’s legal consequences?
Did B disappear voluntarily?
Did B’s disappearance itself lead the authorities to suspect A?
Was B’s voluntary disappearance motivated by something A did after they reunited?
Did authorities suspect A because of evidence or information independent of B’s disappearance?
Did B plan the disappearance in advance?
Was the independent information that led authorities to suspect A based on something A had done or said?
Did authorities suspect A because of a statement A made to them about B?
Did A falsely tell the authorities that A had killed B?
Was A’s false claim meant to mislead investigators about B’s whereabouts?
Was A’s false claim motivated by a desire to protect B?
Was A’s false confession motivated by guilt over A’s earlier role in disrupting B’s life?
Was A’s false confession intended to achieve a particular goal for A?
Was A trying to avoid a legal consequence for A?
Was A’s goal in confessing to cause someone else to take a particular action?
Was A trying to induce someone other than B to take a particular action?
Was A trying to induce B to end the disappearance?
Was B trying to avoid an immediate danger to themself?
Was B’s disappearance intended to make a permanent break from their previous life?
Did A expect B to respond to the confession by contacting A directly?
Was A trying to get B to reappear publicly or contact someone other than A?
Was A trying to get B to resume their marriage?
Was A hoping B would reappear and tell the authorities that A’s confession was false?
Did the parent’s crime or its legal consequences contribute to B’s decision to disappear?
Was B’s disappearance partly motivated by fear of being implicated in the parent’s crime?
Was B’s disappearance motivated by emotional distress over the parent’s crime or its consequences?
Was A hoping B’s reappearance would change A’s circumstances in some way beyond correcting the false confession?
Was the additional change A hoped for primarily personal or emotional?
Was A’s additional personal goal to resolve A’s own feelings about B?
Was A’s additional personal goal related to B’s emotional well-being?
Was A hoping to personally comfort or support B if B reappeared?
Did B know about the parent’s crime before A disclosed it?
Was B’s parent’s crime committed against a person?
Did B’s parent’s crime result in the victim’s death?
Was the person killed by B’s parent someone personally close to B?
Was B’s emotional distress specifically about the victim’s death, rather than the consequences for B’s parent?
Did a change in the parent’s circumstances shortly before B disappeared trigger B’s decision to disappear?
Was B’s distress driven by some aspect of how they learned about or understood the crime?
Was B’s distress about how the crime was revealed or understood, rather than about the consequences for their parent?
Was B distressed because A’s disclosure made the crime known to other people, rather than because B learned new details about it?
Did B personally take any action to conceal the parent’s crime before A disclosed it?
Was B distressed by what the crime revealed about their parent’s character, rather than by how the crime became known?
Was the parent’s killing intentional?
Before A disclosed the crime, did B know that their parent had intentionally killed someone?
Did B’s distress come from learning a specific fact about the parent’s conduct that changed B’s view of them?
Was the specific fact that changed B’s view of their parent the parent’s motive for the intentional killing?
Was the fact that changed B’s view of their parent about the circumstances or manner of the killing, rather than the victim’s identity?
Did the fact that changed B’s view concern the parent’s conduct during the killing, rather than something before or after it?
Did the newly learned fact concern an additional act by the parent, beyond the intentional killing itself?
Did the fact that changed B’s view of their parent concern the parent’s attitude toward the victim?
Did the newly learned fact concern whether the victim posed a threat when the parent killed them?
Was the fact that changed B’s view about how the parent treated someone other than the victim?
Did B learn that their parent had concealed an important fact about the killing?
Was the fact that changed B’s view of their parent the identity of the victim?
Did B learn that their parent had committed other intentional killings besides this one?
Was the fact that changed B’s view of their parent something beyond the fact that their parent intentionally killed someone?
Did B’s disappearance follow learning that their parent had intentionally killed someone?
Did B learn the specific fact that changed their view of their parent from A’s disclosure?
Was B’s changed view triggered by learning that the parent had intentionally killed someone, rather than by learning a separate fact about the parent?
Would learning only that their parent had intentionally killed someone—without any further detail—have changed B’s view of them?
Did B know some aspect of the parent’s crime before A’s disclosure, but learn a different aspect later?
Was the victim’s relationship to B relevant to B’s distress?
Was B distressed because the parent’s killing was motivated by a personal or financial benefit?
Was B distressed because learning of the killing revealed that their parent had committed a serious betrayal of someone they trusted?
Was B distressed to learn that their parent had intentionally killed an innocent person?
Was B’s emotional distress primarily shame about having a parent who had committed murder?
Was B’s disappearance driven primarily by B’s own shame about having a parent who committed murder, rather than by fear of other people’s judgment?
Was B’s disappearance motivated by fear that other people would judge or stigmatize them because their parent had committed murder?
Did fear of other people’s judgment independently contribute to B’s disappearance, apart from B’s own shame?
Did A disclose the crime to authorities before B transferred schools?

At school, A deliberately told the authorities about a murder B’s parent had already committed. The parent faced criminal consequences, and B moved in with a relative, prompting B to transfer schools. The crime and its revelation contributed to B’s shame about having a parent who had committed murder and fear of others’ judgment. Years later, after A and B had reunited, married, and seemed loving, B voluntarily disappeared partly for those reasons. A had not killed B. Hoping B would reappear and tell the authorities the confession was false—and hoping to comfort and support B—A falsely claimed to have killed them. That statement led authorities to suspect and arrest A.
